description:
FILED s473t1 (Opus, the 13-file early-stop triage).  PRE-EXISTING.

REPRO (scratch/s473t1/probe/bareword-postderef.pl):

    no strict 'refs';
    our @foo = (7,8,9); our %foo = (foo=>'oof'); our $foo = 43;
    print join(' ', foo->@*), "\n";        # perl: 7 8 9
                                           # PCL : dies, Undefined subroutine &main::foo

Every spelling agrees in perl and every one dies in PCL:
    foo->@*        7 8 9
    "@{[foo->@*]}" 7 8 9
    "foo"->@*      7 8 9
    foo->@[0,1]    7 8
    foo->@{foo}    oof

The bareword before `->` is a CLASS-NAME string, and `->@*` postfix-derefs
that string as a symbolic array ref.  PCL's callable classifier (#266 family)
answers "call" where it should answer "string": `foo` is not a declared sub
here.  It is NOT an interpolation bug -- the direct form fails too.

COST: perl-tests/postfixderef.t rows 133-135 ('->@* inside "@{...}"',
'->@[ inside "@{...}"', '->@{ inside "@{...}"'), 3 of the file's 7 missing
rows; the other 4 are the DESTROY family.  Three top-level forms abort:
"; PCL recovery: top-level form aborted (recovered): Undefined subroutine
&main::foo called" x3.
subject: A BAREWORD invocant of a postfix deref (`foo->@*`) is compiled as a SUB CALL; perl treats it as a symbolic reference under `no strict refs`
